fields.h1: Build a Culture Survey That Tests Your Values
fields.hero_description: Build a culture survey that scores each value by what employees see at work, with every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_subheading: One prompt with your values and teams gives your employee culture survey each piece below.
fields.feature_1:
Behavior statements for every value

Emergent writes two or three statements per value about things people can watch happen. Ownership becomes: I can fix a problem outside my team without asking for permission first.
fields.feature_2:
Agreement scored by value and team

Each statement is scored as the share of people who agree or strongly agree. Statements roll up to the value they test, and the dashboard can split every value by department or site.
fields.feature_3:
A reporting minimum you choose

Pick the smallest group allowed to see results, such as five people. A team below it shows no scores or comments on any dashboard, though its answers still count in the total.
fields.feature_4:
Open answers grouped by theme

Add an open question, for example the three words that describe working here. The survey sorts the answers into themes, counts them, and keeps each original reply under its theme.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when a team drops below a floor

Set a floor for any statement. When one team falls under it, the survey emails that team's owner or messages them in Slack with the score, the answer count, and the comments.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

The survey, its response tables, and its dashboards are ordinary code. Export them to your GitHub repository on paid plans, host them yourself, or keep changing them by prompt.

fields.tab_content_1:
Of five values, candor comes last

A 240-person software company turns its five values into 15 statements about everyday behavior, and 198 people answer. Candor scores lowest: fewer than half agree with its three statements. Most of the comments under it mention the same weekly leadership review.
fields.tab_content_2:
Line 4 doubts it can report a near miss

Operators and supervisors on five production lines answer a safety culture survey on a shared tablet at shift change. One statement reads: I can report a near miss without being blamed. When under 60% of a line agree, the plant safety manager gets an email with that line's results and comments.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two companies split on who signs off

Six months after Halden Logistics buys Brightwater Labs, both staffs answer the same 16 statements about how work gets done, and each company gets its own column. The widest split is sign-off: most Halden staff say decisions wait for a director, while few at Brightwater do. That gap goes to the integration lead.
fields.tab_content_4:
Three words each from 290 people

Every employee at a 300-person agency gets one open question: which three words describe working here? The 290 people who answer give 870 words, and the survey groups them into themes. Fast leads and siloed comes second. The people team gets the ranked list in Slack, with the answers behind each theme.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Culture Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a culture survey that checks each value against daily behavior and names one change per gap.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Copy the values you already claim
fields.howto_step_1_des: Take your values word for word from the handbook or careers page. Add habits leaders talk about, such as written decisions or no-meeting Fridays. Leave out anything nobody has promised. The survey tests claims, not hopes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write your culture survey questions as statements about something a person could witness, not something they should believe. Candor becomes: people here say so when they disagree with a plan. Keep one idea per statement and avoid leading wording.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A confidential survey ties answers to a roster, which lets reminders and team splits work. An anonymous one stores no identity at all. Choose one, set a reporting minimum of at least five, and state both on the first screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Starting from a culture survey template means editing someone else's values. Write a short brief instead: who answers, your statements, the groups to compare, and any alert rules. Emergent builds the survey, its database, and the dashboards from it.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the draft to about 10 people from different teams and ask which statements they read two ways. Rewrite those before launch. A statement people read two ways gives you a score nobody can act on.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Sort values by agreement and start with the lowest. Then compare groups, since a value that scores well overall can still fail in one department or among newer staff. Read the comments before you decide what a number means.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Change one behavior, then ask again
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share company results within a few weeks of closing. For the weakest value, name one behavior leadership will change and who owns that change. A year later, ask the identical statements again so the two scores line up.

plan.angle: The top 10 is consultancy pages (Culture Index, CCO, Perceptyx), question lists (AIHR, Leapsome), one SurveyMonkey template and an article on culture versus engagement surveys. None turns a company's stated values into statements about behavior people can see, or shows results split where culture breaks: one production line, an acquired company, open-text words. This page keeps culture (shared values and everyday norms) apart from engagement and satisfaction, and shows four working culture surveys a company owns as an app.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Culture Survey That Tests Your Values'; hero 'Build a culture survey that scores each value by what employees see at work, with every answer in a database you own.'

intent.evidence: Searchers want examples, questions and templates: 'Four Culture Survey Examples', step 2 behavior statements, FAQ 4 and 10 give concrete statements, FAQ 6 template contents.

specificity.evidence: HR vocabulary: 'reporting minimum', 'confidential survey ties answers to a roster', 'share of people who agree or strongly agree'.

openers.evidence: Bodies open on full sentences: 'Emergent writes two or three statements per value...', 'Each statement is scored as the share...'.

voice.evidence: Specific, operator voice: 'Ownership becomes: I can fix a problem outside my team without asking for permission first.'

truth.evidence: FAQ 1 checked against the DecisionWise page: 'An employee engagement survey, however, measures the level of employee commitment, motivation, and satisfaction' and 'A culture survey focuses on understanding the organization's values, beliefs, and practices' (present verbatim). FAQ 3 checked against American Data Network: 'Staff speak up if they see something unsafe...' and 'Staff are informed when errors occur...' both present. Emergent claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, code-export, api-connect, alerts, no-caps.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (values tested as observable behavior); D2 hero overlap with employee-benefits-survey 18%, under the line.

faq.evidence: 10 builder-side questions (definition, how to create, safety culture, good questions, honest answers, template, examples, workplace and team culture, five questions); hub link in item 2; links to pulse survey and exit survey.
